identity.name: Srigee DLM Limited
identity.industry: EMS / Plastics & Polymer Compounding — design-led contract manufacturing (injection moulding, mobile assembly, tool room)

summary.oneLiner: Srigee is a sub-INR-100-cr micro-cap, design-led plastics/EMS contract manufacturer (air-cooler moulding for Symphony/Havells, Samsung mobile-assembly job-work via Elentec, plus a nascent "Polymos" polymer-compounding vertical) that just IPO'd (May-2026) and is running at >100% capacity utilisation — so the entire growth story hinges on a single 10,850 sqm new plant (R11A, Greater Noida) targeted for commissioning by ~Aug 15 / pre-Diwali FY27. FY26 delivered INR 72.3 cr revenue / INR 6.87 cr PAT (9.06% margin) with H2 PAT more than doubling YoY; management's *personal* (un-guided, aspirational) targets are ~INR 100 cr FY27 → INR 200-250 cr FY28, contingent entirely on the new facility landing on time.

one-line thesis: Srigee is a sub-INR-100-cr micro-cap, design-led plastics/EMS contract manufacturer (air-cooler moulding for Symphony/Havells, Samsung mobile-assembly job-work via Elentec, plus a nascent "Polymos" polymer-compounding vertical) that just IPO'd (May-2026) and is running at >100% capacity utilisation — so the entire growth story hinges on a single 10,850 sqm new plant (R11A, Greater Noida) targeted for commissioning by ~Aug 15 / pre-Diwali FY27. |---|---|---|---|

> One-offs / context: FIRST earnings call post-IPO (listed 12-May-2026; allotment 31-Mar-2026). ~50% of IPO proceeds utilised by 31-Mar-2026; balance to be deployed this/next quarter. Margin uplift this year partly non-recurring (other income + mobile-line ramp). All forward numbers are explicitly the MD's "personal target," NOT formal guidance.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue (MD's personal target, NOT formal):** FY27 ~INR 100 cr ("lost ~3-4 months / 2 quarters" to plant transition, so conservative); FY28 (Apr'27-Mar'28) ~INR 200-250 cr; new plant peak potential ~INR 200-350 cr; aspiration to eventually reach INR 1,000 cr.
- **Margin:** Too early to quantify ("transitional phase"); will be "on the positive side of existing"; all ratios/margins to grow in proportion to topline, "should not decrease."
- **Capex:** ~INR 24-25 cr capex by ~Mar'27 (apart from land already acquired); total new-plant project ~INR 50 cr. Asset turn at peak ~INR 200 cr on the INR 25 cr capex (mgmt math).
- **Commissioning (KEY WATCH):** New plant R11A (10,850 sqm, ~4x current footprint) — target commercial production ~Aug 15, 2026; realistically "before Diwali" (India construction-delay caveat). Ecotech-10 (2,000 sqm) plot SHELVED — funds redirected to the larger R11A.
- **Polymos:** ~50 MT/month now → ~150 MT/month (3x) post-shift; revenue ~INR 1 cr/month now → INR 2.5-3 cr/month FY27 (~double), 3x next year.
- **Mobile assembly:** Samsung volumes (~10 lakh phones; Srigee <10% share) — sales doubled INR 50 lakh→INR 1 cr/month; 4x space committed; highest-MARGIN vertical.
order book & pipeline:
- No traditional order book (OEM/ODM job-work; quarterly-priced POs). Growth visibility = capacity + customer pipeline.
- **Customer pipeline (post-new-plant):** 3 new ODM/OEM customers in talks; 2 have visited site & informally confirmed business (home-appliances: hand-blender, juicer-mixer-grinder segments). Havells gave informal "LOI-kind" assurance for added space/business. Audit-clearance + space are the only two stated constraints.
- Existing marquee customers: Symphony, Havells, LG, Yamaha, Neelkamal, Elentec (Samsung mobile-assembly route).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Plastic injection moulding & assembly (core):** Air-coolers for OEMs (Symphony, etc.); seasonal (weak Jun-Aug). Largest revenue contributor.
- **Mobile phone assembly (job-work):** Pure job-work for Samsung via Elentec; <10% of Samsung's ~10 lakh/mo volume; sales INR 50L→INR 1 cr/mo (doubled); committed 4x space. Highest-margin vertical (margin-wise, not sales-wise).
- **Polymer compounding ("Polymos"):** 2 yrs old, nascent; 1 twin-screw extruder, ~50 MT/mo; FY26 rev INR 11.257 cr (mfg+trading); installed capacity INR 26 cr. ~25-30% internal/captive (in-house consumption ~35-40 MT/mo). Double benefit: ~INR 10 mfg saving + ~INR 10 trading margin per unit.
- **Tool room & die:** Back-end vertical; under-harnessed potential (per MD). Enables in-house tooling cost savings.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Polymos 3x expansion** (50→150 MT/mo) — back-end margin lever + external trading.
- **Mobile assembly scale-up** — Samsung headroom (currently <10% share); margin-accretive.
- **New consumer-durable categories** — hand-blenders, juicer-mixer-grinders, home appliances (new customers beyond coolers) → customer diversification.
- **Tool room** — flagged as under-utilised optionality.
- **Vertical FAR expansion** — new plant built to FAR 1.5 vs permissible 4 → can expand upward as business grows without new land.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Limited pricing leverage with OEMs ("OEM business is set" — fixed machine tariff/profit/overhead/rejection format). Margin gains come from BACK-END channeling (own tool room + own polymer extrusion) saving ~INR 10/unit, not from customer-side pricing.
- New plant consolidation (4 units → 1) saves duplicated overheads — guard, plant head, housekeeping, generator per site → margin accretive.
- Saved rent (new plant owned vs current rented) flows to income.
- **War / crude → polymer cost shock:** Polymer is a crude by-product; in Feb-Mar prices spiked ~3x. Quarterly-priced POs meant Srigee absorbed the Mar-quarter hit (couldn't reprice mid-quarter); pre-bought heavy polymer in March to cushion. From next quarter, POs reflect current (higher Reliance list) prices, so pass-through normalises.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- New plant R11A (10,850 sqm) — total project ~INR 50 cr; capex ~INR 24-25 cr by Mar'27 (ex-land). Funding = IPO INR 17 cr equity + bank debt (ICICI, ~equiv/higher, ~8-9%) + sale of smaller units' land.
- **Slippage risk is THE key risk:** commissioning target ~Aug 15, realistically pre-Diwali; India contractor-delay caveat explicitly acknowledged. Smaller units to be sold (machines moved, land monetised).
- Ecotech-10 (2,000 sqm) plot SHELVED — capital reallocated to larger R11A (avoid double-shift).
capital allocation:
- 100% of IPO proceeds → plant (50% used by 31-Mar-2026; balance this/next quarter).
- Combination funding: equity (IPO) + debt (ICICI, negotiating ~8.25%) + asset sales (small units).
- No dividend discussion (reinvestment / growth phase; micro-cap).
- Net asset-turn math: ~INR 25 cr capex → ~INR 200 cr peak revenue.
risks & watch-items:
- **Single-asset execution risk:** entire growth thesis depends on ONE new plant commissioning on time; any slippage stalls the FY27/28 ramp (company explicitly "stalled only because no space").
- **Customer concentration:** top-10 ~91% of revenue (down from ~95%); heavy dependency; diversification still aspirational/un-contracted.
- **Forward numbers are NOT guidance:** repeatedly framed as MD's "personal target"; FY27 INR 100 cr / FY28 INR 200-250 cr / plant INR 350 cr are aspirational.
- **Polymer/crude price volatility** (war-linked) — margin squeeze when POs are quarterly-priced and input spikes mid-quarter.
- **OEM pricing power weak** — thin/fixed job-work economics; margin upside depends on back-end integration delivering as planned.
- **Seasonality** — cooler business weak Jun-Aug.
- **Leverage ramp** — taking on ~INR 30-33 cr debt onto a tiny balance sheet; rate negotiation (8.25% vs 9.5%) unresolved.
- **Disclosure maturity:** new listee; this is the first-ever transcript; small unnamed "Management" speakers; numbers occasionally vague/un-bifurcated on the call.
management quality / tone: - First-ever earnings call; MD (Shashi Kant Singh) candid, hands-on, plain-spoken, promoter-driven. Transparent about constraints ("growth stalled only because no space") and about absorbing the polymer cost hit. Repeatedly self-flags forward numbers as "personal targets," which is honest but means low formal accountability. Benchmarks ambition vs listed peers PG Electroplast & Amber ("INR 500 cr on 7,500 sqm") to argue his INR 350 cr on 10,850 sqm is "conservative." Promotional on the INR 1,000 cr aspiration; finance answers were sometimes deferred to junior staff and imprecise. Promised to start posting transcripts every quarter going forward.
non-obvious takeaways:
- This is effectively a pre-scale IPO-funded micro-cap: at >100% utilisation, FY26 numbers are a CEILING on the current asset base — there is no organic growth without the new plant. The investment case is binary on plant commissioning timing.
- The real margin engine is BACK-END integration (Polymos compounding + tool room), not the customer-facing OEM/mobile job-work where pricing is fixed. Polymos doing INR ~1 cr/mo already on one extruder, with 3x capacity coming, is the quiet optionality.
- Mobile assembly (Samsung via Elentec) is the highest-margin vertical and sub-10% penetrated — a credible scale lever if space is given, riding India's smartphone-assembly localisation (PLI) tailwind, but it's pure job-work (low capital, low control).
- Peer-benchmarking against PG Electroplast / Amber signals the MD wants the market to re-rate Srigee toward the listed EMS/durables-ODM multiple — a stretch at this scale/concentration, but the directional read-through (durables ODM/EMS capex cycle) is real.

hero.oneLiner: Srigee is a sub-INR-100-cr micro-cap, design-led plastics/EMS contract manufacturer (air-cooler moulding for Symphony/Havells, Samsung mobile-assembly job-work via Elentec, plus a nascent "Polymos" polymer-compounding vertical) that just IPO'd (May-2026) and is running at >100% capacity utilisation — so the entire growth story hinges on a single 10,850 sqm new plant (R11A, Greater Noida) targeted for commissioning by ~Aug 15 / pre-Diwali FY27. FY26 delivered INR 72.3 cr revenue / INR 6.87 cr PAT (9.06% margin) with H2 PAT more than doubling YoY; management's *personal* (un-guided, aspirational) targets are ~INR 100 cr FY27 → INR 200-250 cr FY28, contingent entirely on the new facility landing on time.
